text:
Dear Dr. Bennett,

Thank you for evaluating Mr. Gregory Hill, a 32-year-old accountant who presents for assessment of skin changes that first appeared earlier this year.

On physical examination, he demonstrates marked, confluent thickening and scaling across both palmar surfaces. The soles of his feet are similarly affected, showing pronounced, diffuse hyperkeratotic plaques over the plantar aspects, particularly over the weight-bearing heels and metatarsal pads. In addition, there are discrete, localized areas of hyperkeratotic, ridged skin on his left forearm and right flank; a preliminary punch biopsy from the flank lesion revealed striking granular degeneration with suprabasal vacuolization.

Importantly, examination of his digits reveals entirely normal nail plate morphology, with no evidence of dystrophy, subungual thickening, or pitting. 

Mr. Hill is otherwise healthy. He is a non-smoker, drinks alcohol only socially, and takes no prescribed medications. A recent trial of over-the-counter 20% urea cream provided minimal symptomatic improvement. His family history is entirely negative for skin conditions, and a general physical exam, including cardiovascular and pulmonary auscultation, was completely unremarkable.

I would be very grateful for your formal assessment and recommendations regarding further management.

Sincerely,

Dr. Julian Vance
